finding: Author Decision Queue v1 subject-currentness accepts an exact governed object version whenever that historical version still exists in the append-only parent aggregate. After the active canonical manuscript advances from V1 to V2, a pending decision bound to V1 is therefore still treated as current even though the queue contract defines a changed bound manuscript identity as a material staleness trigger.
root_cause: parentIdentityCatalog indexes every governed object version present in the parent state.
validateSubjectIdentityRefs tests catalog membership but does not require a governed subject to equal the active pointer binding for its governed object class.
revalidateAgainstParent therefore can advance the queue ledger to the new parent while leaving an old-version pending decision effectively resolvable.
safety_effect: A human choice requested for an old manuscript version could be captured against a materially changed active manuscript unless a stricter current-subject boundary blocks it.

qualified_v1_preservation.rule: Do not modify, relabel, or transfer the exact-SHA Author Decision Queue v1 qualification.

requirements: delegate canonical queue and resolution behavior to Author Decision Queue v1
for governed subject identities, require the exact object version to be the active pointer target for that governed class
allow immutable historical versions to remain stored without treating them as current author-choice targets
after parent revalidation, preserve base queue history and record an additive strict-currentness overlay for requests whose governed subject is no longer active
resolution must fail closed when the exact governed subject is no longer active, including when no prior revalidation was performed
no model/provider/timeout authority and no synthetic author choice
no lifecycle, manuscript, proposal, export-freeze, publication, or provider authority

research_gate.reason: This is an internal exact-version/current-pointer custody defect against an already research-verified author-authority contract.
